name: Major cyber incidents
value: France blames IRGC unit for store sabotage
summary: France blamed an IRGC-linked unit on 9 Nov for October hacks of fridges at about 700 stores that caused fires
state: France attributed the 11–12 Oct sabotage of refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites, which caused at least 15 fires, to Shahid Kaveh, a unit tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guards (BleepingComputer, 9 Nov; The Record). Iran rejected the accusation on 10 Nov. Searches to 15 Nov found no new national-scale attack on critical infrastructure, but this destructive state-attributed attack, announced within the past week, keeps the Alert.
for_you: Retailers and operators of internet-connected building and refrigeration controls are most exposed. Attributions like this tend to bring sanctions talk and fresh government advisories. The NCSC publishes guidance on securing operational technology and remote access.
rubric_hit: Destructive state-attributed attack: France attributes sabotage of ~700 sites' refrigeration to IRGC unit (9 Nov)

sources.title: BleepingComputer — France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
